title: Radiation therapy quality assurance (RT QA) of adjuvant fractionated radiotherapy for WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma in the ROAM/EORTC1308 trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: ROAM/EORTC-1308 is an international (Europe and Australasia) phase III randomised controlled trial (RCT) comparing radiotherapy (60Gy/30#) to observation after surgery for WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma. The treatment plans of all the patients randomised to radiotherapy were reviewed and approved prior to treatment delivery. Pretrial credentialling included outlining and planning a benchmark case. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Variations from the guidelines were noted in QA reports both for the Benchmark Case (BM) and for on-trial Individual Case Reviews (ICRs). After the trial, the QA reports were used to analyse the variations in the BM and ICRs. A random 10% of the ICRs were reviewed again independently. In all cases the reviewer agreed with the original decision. RESULTS: 58 centres opened, of which 56 centres (20 UK, 25 EORTC, 11 TROG) submitted BM. Two centres did not undergo radiotherapy credentialling and closed without recruiting any patients. Resubmissions were: 4 (7%) for outlining and 11 (20%) for planning. During the trial 66 patients at 28 centres received radiotherapy, (median 2 patients per site). Resubmissions for ICRs were: 31 (48%) sets of outlines (3 cases twice) and 12 (18%) treatment plans (1 plan twice). There were 28 instances of major variations in the ICR outlines and 14 in the ICR plans. CONCLUSIONS: For complex radiotherapy of uncommon tumours, a pre-trial QA is insufficient and prospective ICRs of all patients are required. The consistent high-quality radiotherapy in ROAM/EORTC1308 ensures the primary outcome is robust and that there was no variation in radiotherapy treatment across sites.
